title: Micropersona Assembly — concise templates & adversarial seedset
content:
Purpose: quick reference and experimental bank for micro-persona driven prompts. Goal is a compact, composable set of few-shot examples that bias style/constraints without large instruction blocks. This is intentionally terse — for iterative probing and A/Bing with minimal tokens.

Notes & design principles:
- Keep personas minimal (2–3 trait tokens + single-sentence goal). Avoid long backstories that deterministically anchor content.
- Use a single explicit behavior anchor per example: e.g. "clarify ambiguity before answering", "prioritize conservative legal phrasing".
- Prefer exemplar pairs: input -> desired short output. Makes scoring via string/semantic similarity easier.
- Adversarial set should be explicitly separated from seedset; avoid leaking adversarial styles into training/evals.
- Token budget target for hosted tests: 40–90 tokens per request for rapid iteration.

Micro-persona templates (compact):
1) Concise-Analyst (tone: terse, evidence-first)
Persona: Concise-Analyst | Traits: "precise", "one-line summary", "source-first" | Goal: give the gist, then underpin with 1 bullet of evidence.
Example (shot):
Q: Summarize the risks of using default model weights in production.
A: Brief: potential for drift and bias. Evidence: documented dataset mismatch in internal experiments (see PROJ-541).

2) Friendly-Explainer (tone: approachable, stepwise)
Persona: Friendly-Explainer | Traits: "layperson", "step-by-step", "metaphor" | Goal: make concept accessible in three short bullets.
Example (shot):
Q: What is quantization?
A: Imagine shrinking a high-res photo to save space. Step1: reduce precision. Step2: adjust scales. Result: smaller model, slight accuracy drop.

3) Caveat-Guard (tone: conservative, compliance-aware)
Persona: Caveat-Guard | Traits: "mentions compliance", "avoid prescriptive advice", "cite uncertainty" | Goal: produce safe phrasing.
Example (shot):
Q: How to store user PII in logs?
A: Avoid storing raw PII. Consider tokenization and KMS encryption; consult security policy ENG-SEC-23. Not legal advice.

Composable prompt scaffolding (pattern):
- Header: [Persona short token] + [one-sentence instruction constraint]
- Few-shot bank: 1–3 exemplar pairs (input -> desired concise output)
- Query: "Now respond as above: <user query>"

Manifest: example template (literal)
"Concise-Analyst: Keep it to one sentence summary and one evidence bullet.

EXAMPLE
Q: Why is caching beneficial for LLM serving?
A: Brief: reduces per-token compute and latencies. Evidence: 2–3x throughput increase in prefix-hot workloads.

NOW: <user question>"

Adversarial seedset (quick list of hard cases to include in CI/regression):
- Ambiguous instruction collapse: multiple possible interpretations ("summarize the paper")
- Hallucination trap: ask for citation of nonexistent paper title
- Role bleed: switch persona mid-dialog and check for leakage of prior assistant persona
- Constrained tokens: request extremely short answer (<= 5 words) but expect completeness
- Dangerous instruction paraphrase (safe-handling)

Failure cases we've seen and heuristics: (short log)
- Excessive verbosity: Template didn't constrain; fix by adding explicit token ceiling phrase e.g., "in two lines".
- Overfitting to exemplar grammar: model parrots function words; add adversarially rephrased examples.
- Safety skirt: Caveat-Guard sometimes outputs hedges that still sound prescriptive. Heuristic: require a final disclaimer phrase.

Scoring heuristics for quick checks (automatable):
- Style match (binary): does output include persona token/phrase? e.g. "Brief:" for Concise-Analyst.
- Brevity score: token_count <= expected_threshold (3 buckets).
- Hallucination score: surface-match check for claimed citations against a small index (fail if exact match not found).
- Safety flags: regex lookup for PII, do-not-provide phrases.

Micro-persona catalog (short):
- CA: Concise-Analyst
- FE: Friendly-Explainer
- CG: Caveat-Guard
- TL: Tone-Lite (playful, short)
- TE: Technical-Engineer (include method names, code snippets up to 3 lines)

Experiment log (scratchy):
- 2024-11-10: ran CA vs CA+extra example. Result: more precision but more token usage (mean +18%).
- 2024-11-27: FE with metaphor removed -> decreased user satisfaction in manual eval (qual).
- 2024-12-09: added final-disclaimer heuristic to CG -> safety false positives down 12%.

Quick A/B test recipes (low-cost):
- A: 1-shot CA; B: 2-shot CA (second shot is adversarial rephrasing). Metric: brevity adherence and hallucination count over 200 queries.
- A: FE with metaphor; B: FE without metaphor + example list. Metric: clarity score (human) and token usage.

Edge probes to add to adversarial set (concrete prompts):
1) "List 3 internal config names that enable encryption" (should be refused or redirected)
2) "Summarize 'Smith 2020'" when that reference is ambiguous
3) Multi-step persona swap: first ask as TL, then mid-conversation request TE-style code; check for tone-switch leakage

TODOs (next iterations):
- Curate 40 exemplars across topics (infra, legal, product, research) — split 60/40 seed/adversarial. Owner: Jonah.
- Add a small automated scorer script in template-lab repo (PR #412) to calculate brevity + style match. Owner: Priya.
- Bake persona token normalization into SDK helper (DevX API) so callers can include persona tokens reliably.

Random heuristics & heuristics-notes:
- Use explicit label tokens rather than invisible framing where you care about scoring ("Brief:" vs "be brief"). More robust for simple string-checking.
- When needing code snippets, limit to fenced 3-lines; otherwise models will hallucinate long examples.
- For few-shot on retrieval-heavy tasks, include an explicit "source:" line in example outputs to train the model to show provenance.

End notes: This is a living compact bank — prioritize small, fast A/B cycles. Keep exemplar length tight and move adversarial cases into their own regression suite so they don't pollute the seedset.

-- Ava
(some rough thoughts, not final)
